A drive over a task whose checkout an earlier `f10 start` had opened could
skip it without a word: Herdr opened a second workspace on the same path,
the drive then read the leftover one by path, and the cancelled run's state
ended the task inside `send` with nothing printed until the final report.

- start and drive adopt a workspace Herdr already shows instead of asking
  Herdr to open the checkout again: the one with an agent, else the first;
  any other is named in a note with the command that closes it
- drive addresses the task's workspace by id from then on
- run state recorded before drive started the task's agent is ignored: the
  agent that wrote it is gone
- every end (halt, ask, done) prints when it happens, and a workspace that
  never shows an agent halts after the start window instead of being polled
  until the drive ends

  and runs nothing; wrappers relay `f10 <cmd> --help`. The seed hook skips
  it, so the badge keeps the last real run.

  --help, --dry-run or --driven.
- Taglines that restated the description are gone.
